def D7 (N : S1 X Y) (n m : N.A1) : Prop :=
  ∃ (σ σ' : N.D1) (x : X), (∀ k, k ≠ m → σ k = σ' k) ∧ N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x

def D8 (N : S1 X Y) (m n : N.A1) : Prop := N.D7 n m

def D9 (N : S1 X Y) : Prop := ∀ n, ¬ Relation.TransGen N.D8 n n

def D10 (N : S1 X Y) : Prop := ∃ n, Relation.TransGen N.D8 n n

Explicitly, there exist σ, σ' : N.D1 and x : X such that σ and σ' agree at every k ≠ m in N.A1, while N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x. Again, m and n need not be distinct (so a self-loop D8 N n n is possible).

The target consists of four proposition definitions parameterized by types X and Y and a structure N : S1 X Y (which supplies a finite type N.A1, a type family N.A3 : N.A1 → Type, an initial assignment N.a4, an update function N.a5 : (n : N.A1) → N.D1 → X → N.A3 n where N.D1 is the type of dependent functions (m : N.A1) → N.A3 m, and an output function N.a6). None of the four definitions assert or prove a theorem; each defines a proposition:

1. D7 N n m (for n, m : N.A1): Defines the proposition that there exist two assignments σ, σ' : N.D1 (each mapping every k : N.A1 to a value in N.A3 k) and an element x : X such that (i) for every k : N.A1 with k ≠ m, σ k = σ' k, and (ii) N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x. That is, varying the assignment only at coordinate m can change the value of N.a5 at n for some x : X. Note that σ and σ' range over all of N.D1 (they are not required to be reachable from N.a4), n and m are not required to be distinct, and N.a4 and N.a6 are not involved.

2. D8 N m n (for m, n : N.A1): Defines the binary relation on N.A1 obtained by reversing the arguments of D7, namely N.D7 n m. Explicitly, there exist σ, σ' : N.D1 and x : X such that σ and σ' agree at every k ≠ m in N.A1, while N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x. Again, m and n need not be distinct (so a self-loop D8 N n n is possible).

3. D9 N: Defines the proposition that for every n : N.A1, it is not the case that Relation.TransGen N.D8 n n holds—that is, there is no n : N.A1 and no sequence c_0, c_1, ..., c_k in N.A1 of length k ≥ 1 with c_0 = n, c_k = n, and N.D8 c_i c_(i+1) for every 0 ≤ i < k. Because the transitive closure requires at least one step (k ≥ 1), zero-step paths are excluded while length-1 self-loops (N.D8 n n, i.e., N.D7 n n) are counted and therefore ruled out by D9 N. (If N.A1 or X is empty, D9 N holds vacuously.)

4. D10 N: Defines the proposition that there exists an n : N.A1 such that Relation.TransGen N.D8 n n holds—that is, there exist n : N.A1 and a chain n = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = n in N.A1 with k ≥ 1 steps such that N.D8 c_i c_(i+1) holds for each 0 ≤ i < k. As with D9, a single-step self-loop (k = 1, i.e., N.D8 n n) counts as a witness to D10 N, whereas a zero-step chain (k = 0) does not, and the definition depends on all assignments in N.D1 and all inputs in X without referencing reachability from N.a4 or the function N.a6.

divergences.description: Causal structure is reduced to the unweighted binary dependency graph D8 (whether varying unit m's state can change unit n's next state). In [P-D51a], 'causal structure' refers more broadly to how a system's elements interact (e.g., the full causal mechanisms, functional rules, or transition probabilities underlying IIT's ϕ), and the definitions also omit input-to-unit and unit-to-output dependencies.

The definitions are restricted to the discrete-time, deterministic, synchronous, finite-unit model S1 (where every inter-unit dependency has a one-step lag), whereas the source passages give no formal definition and speak informally of general physical or neural systems that may be continuous-time, asynchronous, or stochastic.

Dependence (D7) is quantified over all joint states σ, σ' : N.D1 and all inputs x : X, ignoring whether those states are reachable from the initial state N.a4 and whether the participating units affect the output N.a6. Consequently, a cycle solely in unreachable states or in units decoupled from the output still counts as recurrent (D10), while an empty input type X (or an empty unit state space) makes D7 vacuously false and classifies every system as feedforward (D9). (Judging dependence over all joint states is declared by the author and aligns with counterfactual causal-structure notions, though the source passages do not specify it.)

D9 and D10 form an exhaustive binary partition (acyclicity vs. existence of any directed cycle of length ≥ 1) that settles boundary cases not specified in the informal source passages: a single unit with a self-loop counts as recurrent (D10), and a system with no units or no inter-unit dependencies counts as feedforward (D9).

judgement.summary: The definitions faithfully formalize the feedforward/recurrent distinction as acyclicity versus existence of a directed cycle (including self-loops) in the inter-unit dependency graph. The caveats are minor idealizations inherent in formalizing informal notions: narrowing 'causal structure' to a binary edge relation on discrete-time deterministic units, quantifying over all (including unreachable) joint states and inputs, and fixing boundary cases left open by the source passages.
